title: Cardholder Liability for Unauthorized Transactions on the Paystride Visa Payroll Card Account
content:
For an unauthorized-transaction dispute on the Paystride Visa Payroll Card Account, the cardholder's liability is the part of the unauthorized amount that is not credited.

**Visa Zero Liability.** When the plan applies Visa Zero Liability and the transaction was a purchase processed over the Visa network, liability is zero. This Visa policy overrides the Regulation E amounts below. It does not cover ATM or teller cash withdrawals.

**Regulation E amounts.** *Original wording, no longer in force:* "Otherwise liability is the lesser of the unauthorized amount and the liability cap for a timely report when the cardholder reported the loss or theft within the timely-report period in business days after the date they learned of the loss, and the lesser of the unauthorized amount and the liability cap for a later report when reported later; unauthorized transfers that posted more than the error notice window in calendar days after the history access date and before the report may be the cardholder's in full."

**Current wording:** Otherwise, when the cardholder reported the loss or theft within the timely-report period in business days after the date they learned of the loss, liability is the lesser of the unauthorized amount and the liability cap for a timely report. When the report came later, it is the lesser of the unauthorized amount and the liability cap for a later report. Unauthorized transfers that posted more than the error notice window in calendar days after the history access date, and before the report, may be the cardholder's in full. On a claim that one of the lost or stolen card claim schedules of the Paystride Visa Payroll Card Account (the signed claim, claim reversal and final claim credit schedules for the Premier and Elite plans and for the Advantage plan) prices, that schedule states its own.

**One loss, one liability.** *Original wording, no longer in force:* "Liability is counted once across all unauthorized transactions from the same loss or theft, applied in posting order." **Current wording:** Liability is counted once across all unauthorized transactions from the same loss or theft, applied in posting order. On a claim one of those schedules prices, that schedule states its own.

**Card not lost or stolen.** The two caps apply only when the card itself was lost or stolen. When it was not, as with unauthorized use while the card is still in hand, liability is zero, except for transfers that posted after that late-notice window and before the report.

## Hypothetical cases (outside those schedules; timely cap 50.00, later cap 500.00)

| Unauthorized amount | Transaction | Report | Liability |
|---|---|---|---|
| 320.00 | purchase over Visa, Visa Zero Liability applied | any | 0.00 |
| 320.00 | ATM withdrawal, card stolen | within the period | 50.00 |
| 320.00 | ATM withdrawal, card stolen | later | 320.00 |
| 35.00 | ATM withdrawal, card lost | within the period | 35.00 |
| 320.00 | ATM withdrawal, card still in hand | within the period | 0.00 |

Under the posting-order rule, two unauthorized ATM withdrawals of 30.00 and 45.00 from one loss reported on time bear 50.00 in all: 30.00 on the first posted and 20.00 on the second.

Liability is counted once across all unauthorized transactions from the same loss or theft, applied in posting order.
